:::{#exr-epe-three-sources}
#### Expected squared prediction error from three sources

Let $\paren{\newpredvar, \newoutvar}$ be a [new observation](#def-new-observation) relative to the random [training set](#def-training-set) $\trainset$.
Suppose the new observation has $\newpredvar = \predvar$.
A [prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) $\predvalf{\predvar}$ at $\predvar$ has
squared [bias](#def-prediction-bias) $\sqf{\bias{\predvalf{\predvar}}} = 1$
and [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) $\Var{\predvalf{\predvar}} = 2$.
The [noise](#def-noise) of $\newoutvar$ has [population variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) $\varpar = 3$.

1. What is the [expected squared prediction error](#def-epe) $\epe{\fitproc}{\nobs}{\predvar}$?
2. If we could remove all bias and all variance of $\predvalf{\predvar}$,
   what would the expected squared prediction error at $\predvar$ be?
3. Which of the three quantities
   (squared bias, variance of $\predvalf{\predvar}$, $\varpar$)
   can a better prediction method reduce,
   and which cannot?

:::
